page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ae.large is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at a base clock of 3.4 GHz. The instance configuration provisions 2 vCPUs derived from a single dedicated physical core via simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). It features 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with instruction support including AVX-512 (foundation, VNNI, and BF16) and hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The server is allocated 8.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of the general-purpose class. There is no bundled local storage, necessitating reliance on network-attached cloud storage volumes. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps, and no dedicated GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark data reflects strong single-core compute performance, placing in the top quartile with a Geekbench single-core score of 2006.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3111.39. However, aggregate parallel throughput remains limited by the 2-vCPU hardware footprint. Multi-core stress-ng (3112.08) and Geekbench multi-core (2501.0) scores fall into the lower quartile. Similarly, high-concurrency benchmarks show constraints, with PassMark database operations and static web serving throughput scoring in the lower percentiles.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g8ae.large offers dedicated execution resources and modern Zen 4 microarchitecture efficiency at an entry-level resource profile. It is well-fitted for low-concurrency backend services, single-threaded batch processing, lightweight microservices, and development environments that benefit from modern instruction sets without requiring heavy parallel capacity.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ae.large is a general-purpose instance featuring an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz with 2 dedicated vCPUs spanning 1 physical core. It provides 8.0 GB of RAM, a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and no bundled local storage or GPUs. The architecture supports modern extensions including AVX-512 and hardware cryptographic instructions. Benchmark results highlight strong single-thread capability, ranking in the top quartile for Geekbench single-core performance. Conversely, multi-core throughput and high-concurrency database operations fall into lower performance tiers due to the dual-thread ceiling. This hardware profile is appropriate for lightweight general-purpose computing, modest microservices, and development workloads with low concurrent load.
